results.name: medium-mstp-pair-root-baseline
results.title: Baseline · MSTP, MLAG pair as root
results.action: Reset the data bridge on all three CHRs over management SSH with protocol-mode=mstp, priority 0x1000 on both MLAG peers and 0x8000 on the access switch. Then run numbered 100 ms pings for 4 s in both VLAN 110 and both bypass directions and read back bridge, MLAG, RSTP and LACP state. No fault is applied.

witness.role: Dual-attached access switch and external RSTP root candidate

c1.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 1

outside_delivery.status: not applicable: the Medium lab has no host outside the conversation

host_table.status: not available: no fault was executed, so there is no recovery window

phases.name: Baseline
phases.expected: Both MLAG peers are connected and use the MLAG primary's system ID as the shared RSTP bridge ID, so both show as root bridge with root ID 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11. The access switch picks its non-edge uplink bond as root port and all VLAN 110 ports forward. RSTP BPDUs from that root reach the access switch, and all four streams deliver with zero loss.

results.title: One-way calibration · MSTP, MLAG pair as root
results.action: After the RSTP pair-root bridge reset and baseline gate, the runner adds a tc ingress filter on host 2's eth3 that drops bypass-forward echo requests (stream 301) for 2 s. It then removes the filter and observes 3 s of settling and a 3 s recovery window.

phases.name: One-way bypass cut
phases.expected: The filter drops only stream 301's echo requests at host 2's bypass port, outside the MLAG fabric. Stream 301 shows exactly one gap, with every request sent, and the gap's bounds enclose the measured 1.9–2.3 s filter interval. The reverse bypass and both VLAN 110 directions lose nothing.

results.name: medium-mstp-pair-root-reboot-secondary
results.title: MLAG secondary reboot · Medium lab, MSTP, MLAG pair as root
results.action: Resets all three bridges over management SSH with protocol-mode=mstp, priority 0x1000 on CHR 1 and CHR 2 and 0x8000 on the access switch. It requires a loss-free baseline with root ID 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11 in the access switch's BPDUs. It then reboots CHR 2 (MLAG secondary) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

witness.name: dc1-access-switch1
witness.role: Dual-attached access switch and external RSTP root candidate

c1.name: dc1-traffic-host1
c1.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 1

c2.name: dc1-traffic-host2
c2.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 2

outside_delivery.status: not applicable: the Medium lab has no host outside the conversation

first_lines.line: <28>Nov 24 13:27:38 dc1-core-mlag1 bridge,warning MLAG: remote heartbeat timeout

phases.name: Secondary down
phases.expected: CHR 1 keeps the shared system ID, which is both the RSTP bridge ID and the LACP system ID, so the access switch still sees root 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11 and its uplink stays the forwarding root port. The virtual links keep carrier, so the access switch and traffic host 2 drop their member to CHR 2 at the LACP short timeout (3 × 1 s). Only traffic hashed to that member sees brief loss.

phases.name: Secondary back
phases.expected: CHR 2 keeps its bond members out of the bond until the MLAG system ID syncs (mlag-init-delay), then adds them under the unchanged shared system ID. The root ID and the access switch's forwarding uplink do not change, so loss is brief or none.

results.name: medium-mstp-pair-root-reboot-primary
results.title: MLAG primary reboot · Medium lab, MSTP, MLAG pair as root
results.action: Resets all three bridges over management SSH with protocol-mode=mstp, priority 0x1000 on CHR 1 and CHR 2 and 0x8000 on the access switch. It requires a loss-free baseline with root ID 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11 in the access switch's BPDUs. It then reboots CHR 1 (MLAG primary) with `/system reboot`, waits for the guest uptime to reset and keeps probing for 16 s plus a 3 s recovery window.

witness.name: dc1-access-switch1
witness.role: Dual-attached access switch and external RSTP root candidate

c1.name: dc1-traffic-host1
c1.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 1

c2.name: dc1-traffic-host2
c2.role: Linux VLAN 110 and bypass probe host 2

outside_delivery.status: not applicable: the Medium lab has no host outside the conversation

phases.name: Primary down
phases.expected: CHR 2 reverts its MLAG bonds to its own LACP system ID and the access switch and traffic host 2 renegotiate LACP, with brief loss. The MLAG pair must stay RSTP root (0x1000 against 0x8000), and CHR 2's access-uplink and the access switch's uplink must keep forwarding.

phases.name: Primary back
phases.expected: CHR 1 keeps its bond members out of the bond until the MLAG system ID syncs (mlag-init-delay). It rejoins as MLAG primary and restores the shared system ID as LACP system ID and RSTP bridge ID, and partners renegotiate LACP with brief loss. The access switch must again see root 0x1000.02:00:00:21:00:11 with its uplink forwarding.
